general practitioners (GPS) are less likely to manage some cancers with a ‘referrral only’ or ‘investigation only’ option, and are more likely to manage some other cancers with a ‘refferal only’ or ‘refferal with investigation’ option.

GPs are not managing patients with cancer symptoms according to guidelines.

GPs are less likely to refer or investigate patients with symptoms of breast cancer and prostate cancer than patients with symptoms of colorectal cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the management of cancer patients by GPs is highly variable.
